questions.topic: Engineering mechanics, stresses, SFD/BMD & bending
questions.question: A steel bar 2 m long and 500 mm² in cross-section carries an axial tensile load of 100 kN. If E = 200 GPa, the elongation is
questions.explanation: δ = PL/AE = (100×10³ × 2000)/(500 × 2×10⁵) = 2 mm. (Mixing up GPa and MPa gives 0.2 or 20.)

questions.topic: Engineering mechanics, stresses, SFD/BMD & bending
questions.question: For a material with E = 200 GPa and Poisson's ratio 0.3, the bulk modulus K is about
questions.explanation: K = E/3(1 − 2ν) = 200/(3 × 0.4) ≈ 166.67 GPa. (E/2(1 + ν) ≈ 76.92 GPa is the shear modulus G.)

questions.topic: Engineering mechanics, stresses, SFD/BMD & bending
questions.question: A simply supported beam of span 6 m carries a uniformly distributed load of 10 kN/m over the whole span. The maximum bending moment is
questions.explanation: M_max = wL²/8 = 10 × 36/8 = 45 kN·m at mid-span. (wL²/2 = 180 is the cantilever value; wL²/12 = 30 is the fixed-end moment.)

questions.question: For a beam of rectangular cross-section, the ratio of maximum shear stress to average shear stress is
questions.explanation: τ_max = 1.5 τ_avg for a rectangle (at the neutral axis). For a solid circular section it is 4/3 ≈ 1.33.

questions.topic: Engineering mechanics, stresses, SFD/BMD & bending
questions.question: A point of contraflexure is most likely to occur in
options: a simply supported beam with a central point load
a cantilever with a point load at the free end
a simply supported beam with a uniformly distributed load
questions.explanation: Contraflexure is where the bending moment changes sign. In an overhanging beam the moment is sagging between the supports and hogging over the overhang, so it passes through zero.

questions.topic: Engineering mechanics, stresses, SFD/BMD & bending
questions.question: Assertion (A): The stress produced by a suddenly applied load is twice that produced by the same load applied gradually. Reason (R): For a suddenly applied load, the work done by the load (P × δ) equals the strain energy stored (½ × σ × A × δ).
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.explanation: Both are true and R explains A: Pδ = ½σAδ gives σ = 2P/A, twice the gradual-loading value P/A.

questions.topic: Principal stresses, columns, torsion, springs & shells
questions.question: At a point, σx = 80 MPa, σy = 20 MPa and τxy = 40 MPa. The principal stresses are
questions.explanation: σ₁,₂ = (σx + σy)/2 ± √[((σx − σy)/2)² + τ²] = 50 ± √(30² + 40²) = 50 ± 50, giving 100 and 0 MPa. Maximum shear stress = 50 MPa.

questions.topic: Principal stresses, columns, torsion, springs & shells
questions.question: Compared with the same column hinged at both ends, the Euler crippling load of a column fixed at both ends is
questions.explanation: Effective length: both ends hinged — L; both fixed — L/2. Since P = π²EI/Le², halving Le multiplies P by 4. A column fixed at one end and free at the other (Le = 2L) carries ¼ of the hinged load.

questions.question: A thin cylindrical shell of 1 m diameter and 10 mm wall thickness is subjected to an internal pressure of 2 MPa. The circumferential (hoop) stress is
questions.explanation: σ_c = pd/2t = 2 × 1000/(2 × 10) = 100 MPa. The longitudinal stress pd/4t = 50 MPa is half of it.

questions.topic: Fluid statics, kinematics, dynamics & pipe flow
questions.question: The gauge pressure at a depth of 10 m in fresh water (ρ = 1000 kg/m³, g = 9.81 m/s²) is
questions.explanation: p = ρgh = 1000 × 9.81 × 10 = 98,100 Pa = 98.1 kPa (gauge). Adding atmospheric pressure (≈101.3 kPa) would give absolute pressure.

questions.topic: Fluid statics, kinematics, dynamics & pipe flow
questions.question: For a vertical rectangular plane surface whose top edge lies at the free water surface, the centre of pressure is located at a depth of (H = height of the plane)
questions.explanation: h_cp = h̄ + I_G/(A h̄) = H/2 + (bH³/12)/(bH × H/2) = H/2 + H/6 = 2H/3. The centre of pressure is always below the centroid.

questions.topic: Fluid statics, kinematics, dynamics & pipe flow
questions.question: Water flows through a pipe that reduces from 200 mm to 100 mm diameter. If the velocity in the larger pipe is 2 m/s, the velocity in the smaller pipe is
questions.explanation: By continuity, A₁V₁ = A₂V₂ and A ∝ d², so V₂ = 2 × (200/100)² = 8 m/s.

questions.topic: Fluid statics, kinematics, dynamics & pipe flow
questions.question: Water (kinematic viscosity 1 × 10⁻⁶ m²/s) flows at 0.5 m/s in a 50 mm pipe. The flow is
questions.explanation: Re = VD/ν = 0.5 × 0.05/10⁻⁶ = 25,000 — far above about 4,000, so the flow is turbulent. Pipe flow is laminar below about 2,000.

questions.topic: Fluid statics, kinematics, dynamics & pipe flow
questions.question: Using Darcy–Weisbach with f = 0.02, the head loss in a 100 m long pipe of 100 mm diameter carrying water at 2 m/s is about
questions.explanation: h_f = fLV²/2gD = 0.02 × 100 × 4/(2 × 9.81 × 0.1) ≈ 4.08 m. (Here f is the Darcy friction factor; with Fanning's f the formula is 4fLV²/2gD.)

questions.topic: Fluid statics, kinematics, dynamics & pipe flow
questions.question: Match the device with what it measures: A. Venturimeter B. Pitot tube C. Piezometer D. Rotameter — 1. Velocity at a point 2. Discharge in a pipe (by pressure difference) 3. Static pressure (low, gauge) 4. Discharge (variable-area)
questions.explanation: Venturimeter — discharge from the pressure difference across a throat; Pitot tube — point velocity from stagnation pressure; piezometer — small gauge pressures; rotameter — variable-area flow meter.

questions.topic: Fluid statics, kinematics, dynamics & pipe flow
questions.question: For fully developed laminar flow in a circular pipe, the ratio of maximum velocity to mean velocity is
questions.explanation: The Hagen–Poiseuille profile is parabolic with u_max = 2 × u_mean. For turbulent flow the profile is flatter, with u_max ≈ 1.2 × u_mean.

questions.topic: Fluid statics, kinematics, dynamics & pipe flow
questions.question: A floating body is in stable equilibrium when its metacentre is
options: coincident with its centre of gravity
coincident with its centre of buoyancy
questions.explanation: Positive metacentric height (GM > 0) means a restoring couple when the body tilts. M coinciding with G is neutral; M below G is unstable.

questions.topic: Hydraulic turbines, pumps & hydro plants
questions.question: Match the turbine with its typical application: A. Pelton wheel B. Francis turbine C. Kaplan turbine — 1. Medium head, medium discharge (mixed flow) 2. High head, low discharge (impulse) 3. Low head, high discharge (axial flow)
questions.explanation: Pelton — impulse turbine for high heads; Francis — mixed-flow reaction turbine for medium heads; Kaplan — axial-flow reaction turbine with adjustable blades for low heads and large flows.

questions.topic: Hydraulic turbines, pumps & hydro plants
questions.question: The specific speed of a hydraulic turbine is given by
questions.explanation: Turbine: Ns = N√P/H^(5/4) (based on power). Centrifugal pump: Ns = N√Q/H^(3/4) (based on discharge). Mixing up the two is the common trap.

questions.topic: Hydraulic turbines, pumps & hydro plants
questions.question: Cavitation in a hydraulic machine occurs when
options: the liquid temperature falls below its freezing point
the local pressure exceeds atmospheric pressure
the velocity of flow becomes zero
the local pressure falls below the vapour pressure of the liquid
questions.explanation: Vapour bubbles form where pressure drops below vapour pressure and collapse violently in higher-pressure zones, pitting the blades. Draft-tube design and adequate NPSH prevent it.

questions.topic: Hydraulic turbines, pumps & hydro plants
questions.question: The main function of a draft tube in a reaction turbine is to
options: prevent water hammer in the penstock
regulate the flow into the runner
increase the pressure at the inlet of the runner
recover kinetic energy at exit and allow the turbine to be set above the tail-race
questions.explanation: The diverging draft tube converts exit kinetic energy into pressure energy (raising the effective head) and lets the runner be placed above the tail-water level without losing head.
